acceptanceCriteria: A decision records whether the converter refuses a cem/0.1 source whose patchSha256 is not the canonical base..target diff digest (new CEM-V1-101 code) or keeps the CEM-V1-104 recorded limit, and the spec cites the choice.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 in the V1-1275 independent review (internal/cem/convert TestCEMV1104ConvertParityCEM01, repository_test.go). The cem/0.1 conformance fixture carries a patchSha256 over an out-of-band patch; verify.Exact accepts it only with those patch bytes. cem/1.0 has no out-of-band patch member, so the converted map verifies REJECT patch-digest-mismatch at the substituted target, the same result verify.Exact gives the source with the canonical diff. Decision 0525 section 4 says the converter never changes a verdict; CEM-V1-104 records this as a limit. The committed corpus (603 maps) holds no cem/0.1 map, so no migrated verdict changes. Question: should the converter refuse such a source with a bounded code when a repository is given, or is the recorded limit sufficient until V1-1278 removes the 0.x readers?
title: cem/0.1 out-of-band patch sources convert to a map that verifies REJECT patch-digest-mismatch
